1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EMR: Elastic MapReduce; DMS: Database Migration Service; ETL: extract, transform, load; JDBC: Java Database Connectivity; SFTP: Secure File Transfer Protocol; FTPS: File Transfer Protocol Secure; FTP: File Transfer Protocol; EFS: Elastic File System; KMS: Key Management Service; SSL: Secure Sockets Layer; AZ: Availability Zone; SCT: Schema Conversion Tool; SDK: software development kit; ORC: Optimized Row Columnar; DPU: data processing unit; REST: representational state transfer; MWAA: Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow; DAG: directed acyclic graph; SNS: Simple Notification Service; SQS: Simple Queue Service; FIFO: first in, first out; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; NAT: network address translation; IAM: Identity and Access Management

  • Read data from batch sources: Amazon S3, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, AWS DMS, Amazon Redshift, AWS Lambda and Amazon AppFlow
  • Pick the configuration options that make a batch load correct, incremental and fast
  • Consume data APIs safely: paging, authentication and retries
  • Start jobs on a schedule (EventBridge, Apache Airflow, cron) or by an event (S3 Event Notifications, EventBridge)
  • Let only the right network addresses reach a data source (allowlists)
  • Handle throttling and rate limits with retries and backoff

2Batch Ingestion: Sources and the Tool That Fits

Running case

Kestrel Freight Loads Its First Data

  • Warehouse systems drop order files into a bucket every night
  • A Salesforce account holds customer records the analysts need
  • The billing database must be copied to the lake without slowing it down
  • A partner publishes fuel prices through a web API
  • Your job: pick the right tool for each source, then run each on time

Batch or streaming

  • Batch: data arrives or is read in groups on a schedule or on an event (hourly files, a nightly export); results are minutes to hours old
  • Streaming: records are read one by one as they arrive (Module 2); results are seconds old
  • Hourly, nightly, daily file, export point to batch; near real time, as it happens, continuous point to streaming

Batch sources and tools (skill 1.1.2)

Source or need Service What to remember
Files already in Amazon S3 AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, AWS Lambda Glue: serverless Spark ETL; EMR: Spark, Hive, Presto clusters or serverless; Lambda: small files and quick steps (15-minute limit)
Relational or NoSQL database (copy or keep in sync) AWS DMS A managed replication server; full load, change data capture (CDC) or both; sources and targets can differ in engine
SaaS application (Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, ServiceNow, SAP and more) Amazon AppFlow No code; flows run on demand, on a schedule or on an event; targets include S3 and Redshift
Amazon Redshift data Redshift UNLOAD to S3, COPY from S3, federated query Glue and EMR can also read Redshift tables over JDBC
Bulk files from on premises AWS DataSync, AWS Transfer Family, AWS Snow Family DataSync: managed online transfer; Transfer Family: SFTP, FTPS and FTP into S3 or EFS; Snow Family: offline devices for very large or disconnected sites
Exam tip

The source decides the tool: SaaS → AppFlow, database → DMS, files in S3 → Glue (serverless) or EMR (cluster control), SFTP partners → Transfer Family, on-premises file shares → DataSync.

AWS DMS in one page

  • DMS is a server in the cloud that runs replication software; you define a source endpoint, a target endpoint and a task
  • Migration types: full load (copy what exists), CDC (ongoing changes), full load plus CDC (copy, then keep in sync)
  • Supports homogeneous (same engine) and heterogeneous (different engine) moves; S3 is a common target for lake ingestion
  • Encrypts data at rest with AWS KMS and in flight with SSL; a backup replication instance can take over on failure (Multi-AZ)
  • Schema conversion is separate: DMS Schema Conversion or AWS SCT convert schemas; DMS moves the data (Module 9)

Amazon AppFlow in one page

  • A fully managed integration service that moves data between SaaS applications and AWS services, without code
  • Triggers: on demand, on a schedule, or on an event (for example Salesforce platform events and change data capture events)
  • Can map, filter, mask and validate fields, partition and aggregate the output files, and catalog the data in the AWS Glue Data Catalog
  • Data can travel privately over AWS PrivateLink instead of the internet
  • Custom connectors (a Python or Java SDK) reach sources that are not built in
Exam tip

"Ingest Salesforce data into S3 or Redshift with the least code" is Amazon AppFlow. "Replicate a production database continuously" is AWS DMS with CDC.

3Configuration Options for Batch Ingestion (skill 1.1.3)

Setting Why it matters
Incremental load Read only new or changed data: Glue job bookmarks, DMS CDC, a watermark (last timestamp or key)
File format and size Columnar (Parquet, ORC) and compressed files read faster and cost less; avoid millions of tiny files
Partitioning Write to partitioned prefixes (for example by date) so queries scan less
Parallelism More workers or DPUs in Glue, more nodes in EMR, parallel load threads in DMS
Retries and idempotency A re-run must not duplicate data: bookmarks, upserts, overwrite of a partition
Batch window Run when the source is quiet; keep the load inside the window

Glue job bookmarks

  • A job bookmark is saved state that lets a Glue job skip data it has already processed on the next scheduled run
  • Options: Enable (track and update), Disable (the default: always read everything), Pause (read incrementally without updating the state)
  • S3 sources: supported formats include JSON, CSV, Avro, XML, Parquet and ORC (Glue 1.0 and later); a file is picked again if its last modified time changed
  • JDBC sources: a bookmark key, by default the primary key, which must increase or decrease sequentially with no gaps
  • Bookmarks need a transformation_ctx on each source and sink in the script and job.commit() at the end
  • Reset or rewind a bookmark to reprocess; Glue does not clean the target files, so write to a new output or de-duplicate
  • State is kept per job: deleting a job deletes its bookmark; changing the source path without changing transformation_ctx makes the job skip files in the new path

Loading Amazon Redshift from S3 (COPY)

  • Use COPY, not many single inserts: it loads in parallel across the cluster's slices
  • Splittable inputs (uncompressed CSV, Parquet, ORC) are split automatically; Redshift splits files of 128 MB or more
  • Not splittable (JSON, or CSV compressed with GZIP): split into files of about 1 MB to 1 GB after compression, and make the number of files a multiple of the number of slices
  • Load from one prefix with one COPY (or a manifest file) so all files load together
Exam tip

"Load a large dataset into Redshift fast" → COPY from S3, many similar-size files, compressed or columnar. "Process only new files each night" → Glue job bookmarks.

4Consuming Data APIs (skill 1.1.4)

  • Many sources (partners, SaaS, internal services) expose data through REST or other APIs; a pipeline calls them from AWS Lambda, AWS Glue (Python jobs or custom connectors), Amazon AppFlow or a container
  • Pull patterns: pagination (follow next-page tokens), incremental requests (since a timestamp), authentication (keys and tokens kept in AWS Secrets Manager), retries with backoff on 429 and 5xx
  • Rate limits are set by the provider; stay under them and spread calls over time
  • To publish your own data to other systems, put Amazon API Gateway in front of Lambda or a data store (Module 3)
  • AWS Data Exchange lets you find and subscribe to third-party datasets and receive them into S3
Exam tip

Secrets in API calls belong in Secrets Manager, never in the code or the job parameters in clear text.

5Schedulers: Time-Based Starts (skill 1.1.5)

Option Use it for Remember
Amazon EventBridge Scheduler A central, scalable schedule that calls 270+ AWS services cron and rate expressions, one-time schedules, time zones, flexible time windows, retries; the recommended way to schedule
EventBridge scheduled rules Older style: rule with a schedule Legacy feature; no faster than every 1 minute
AWS Glue triggers Start jobs and crawlers Types: on-demand, scheduled (cron), conditional (fire when other jobs or crawlers finish with a given status)
Glue crawler schedule Keep the Data Catalog current Time-based; a trigger can start at most two crawlers
Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) Schedules inside DAGs The DAG's schedule interval starts the workflow (Module 4)

EventBridge schedule expressions

  • rate(value unit): for example rate(5 minutes); the unit is singular for 1 (rate(1 hour)) and plural for more (rate(5 hours))
  • cron(fields): six fields: minutes, hours, day-of-month, month, day-of-week, year; times are UTC unless a Scheduler time zone is set
  • You cannot set both day-of-month and day-of-week: use ? in one of them. Example: cron(0 12 * * ? *) runs every day at 12:00 UTC
  • Glue and crawlers also use cron: remember that day 31 does not exist in every month
Exam tip

A schedule starts a job at a time. If the job must start when data arrives, use an event trigger, not a schedule.

6Event Triggers: Start When Something Happens (skill 1.1.6)

  • Amazon S3 Event Notifications publish events such as object created, object removed, restore, replication, lifecycle expiration and transition and tagging
  • Destinations: Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda and Amazon EventBridge; prefix and suffix filters narrow the events to, for example, incoming/ and .csv
  • Delivery is at least once: usually in seconds, sometimes a minute or longer; make consumers idempotent
  • SQS FIFO queues are not a direct S3 destination; route through EventBridge instead
  • Avoid loops: if the function writes to the same bucket that triggers it, it triggers itself; use two buckets or a prefix filter on the incoming path
  • Amazon EventBridge adds content-based filtering, many targets (Step Functions, Glue workflows, Lambda, SQS, SNS and more), archive and replay, and partner and AWS service events
Need Use
One simple reaction to new files (a Lambda) S3 event notification → Lambda
Fan out to several consumers S3 → SNS (→ SQS queues) or EventBridge
Buffer bursts and process at your pace S3 → SQS → consumer
Rich routing, filtering, replay, many targets S3 → EventBridge
Start a Glue workflow or Step Functions run when a file lands EventBridge rule with an S3 event pattern
Exam tip

"Process each file as soon as it arrives" → S3 event → Lambda, or EventBridge → Step Functions or Glue. "Every night at 2 AM" → a schedule.

7Allowlists for Data Sources (skill 1.1.8)

  • Many sources (databases, partner APIs, SaaS) accept connections only from known IP addresses; you give them a fixed address and they allow it
  • Glue, Lambda or an EC2 job inside a VPC reach the internet through a NAT gateway, which has a fixed Elastic IP address: give that address to the source's allowlist
  • For AWS DMS, the source database's security group or firewall must allow the replication instance (its private address in the same VPC, or its public address)
  • For databases in AWS, VPC security groups allow the security group of the job (a reference), which is better than an address list; use VPC endpoints and PrivateLink to avoid the internet
  • Amazon AppFlow can use AWS PrivateLink so the source never sees a public path
Exam tip

"The partner will accept traffic only from one IP address" → run the job in a VPC behind a NAT gateway with an Elastic IP and give the partner that IP.

8Throttling and Rate Limits (skill 1.1.9)

  • Throttling means a service refuses requests above a limit: DynamoDB (ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, ThrottlingException), Amazon RDS (connection and I/O limits), Kinesis (per-shard throughput, Module 2), API Gateway (HTTP 429, default 10,000 requests per second with a 5,000-request burst per account per Region)
  • Exponential backoff with jitter: wait a little longer after each failure (for example up to 50 ms, then 100, then 200) with a random part so many clients do not retry together; AWS SDKs do this automatically
  • Stop retrying after about a minute: if the request still fails, the problem is capacity, not rate, so raise the limit or provision more
  • Batch operations (BatchWriteItem) return unprocessed items: retry those with backoff
  • Fixes at the source of the limit: more capacity (provisioned throughput, on-demand mode, more shards, a bigger instance), spread the keys to avoid a hot partition, buffer with SQS, batch writes, use RDS Proxy to pool connections

Exam tip

"Writes to DynamoDB are throttled during bursts" → on-demand mode or more provisioned capacity, retries with exponential backoff, a better partition key, and SQS in front to smooth the load.

9Exam Q&A

9.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Kestrel Freight wants customer records from Salesforce copied into Amazon S3 every night with as little code as possible. Which service should the data engineer use?

  • AAWS Glue with a custom Python script that calls the Salesforce API
  • BAmazon AppFlow with a scheduled flow
  • CAWS DMS with change data capture
  • DAWS Snow Family
Show the answer

Answer: B. Amazon AppFlow is a managed, no-code integration service for SaaS sources and supports scheduled flows into S3. DMS is for databases, and Snow Family is for bulk offline transfer.

S2A nightly AWS Glue job reads CSV files from an S3 prefix that gets new files every day. The job must process only files that arrived since the last run. What should the engineer enable?

  • AGlue job bookmarks
  • BA larger number of workers
  • CGlue triggers of type conditional
  • DS3 versioning
Show the answer

Answer: A. Job bookmarks keep state between runs so the job skips data it has already processed. Workers add parallelism, conditional triggers chain jobs, and versioning keeps object versions.

S3A data engineer loads a very large set of GZIP-compressed CSV files into Amazon Redshift. Which approach gives the fastest load?

  • ARun one INSERT statement per row from a script that reads the files in turn
  • BRun COPY from S3 on one huge file so that a single slice loads all of it
  • CSplit the data into many files of similar size, a multiple of the slice count, and run one COPY
  • DLoad each file with a separate COPY from a different client at the same time
Show the answer

Answer: C. COPY loads in parallel across slices; GZIP-compressed CSV cannot be split automatically, so many similar-size files (about 1 MB to 1 GB each) in a slice multiple load fastest.

S4A pipeline must start a Lambda function within seconds of each new object arriving in a bucket. Which TWO statements describe a correct design? (Select TWO.)

  • ASend the notification to an SQS FIFO queue directly from S3
  • BSchedule an EventBridge rule every minute to list the bucket
  • CConfigure an S3 event notification for object created events with a Lambda destination
  • DMake the notification consumer idempotent, because delivery is at least once
  • EWrite the function's output into the same bucket and prefix that triggers it
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. S3 event notifications can invoke Lambda, and because delivery is at least once the consumer must handle duplicates. S3 cannot send directly to an SQS FIFO queue, polling is slower and wasteful, and writing to the triggering prefix creates a loop.

S5A partner API accepts requests only from one fixed IP address. The company's AWS Glue job runs in a VPC. What should the data engineer do?

  • AGive the partner the IP address range of the whole AWS Region where the job runs
  • BRun the job in a public subnet that has no route table and no security group
  • CAttach an IAM role to the job so that the partner can recognize the role name
  • DSend the job's outbound traffic through a NAT gateway with an Elastic IP and give that address to the partner
Show the answer

Answer: D. A NAT gateway has a fixed Elastic IP address, so the partner can allowlist it. A whole Region range is not specific, and an IAM role does not change the source address.

S6An ingestion job writes to Amazon DynamoDB and sometimes receives ProvisionedThroughputExceededException during bursts. What is the best FIRST step?

  • ARetry immediately in a tight loop until the request is accepted by the table, and then stop retrying
  • BDelete the table and recreate it with a new name and the same key schema
  • CRetry with exponential backoff and jitter, and review the capacity and the partition key
  • DDisable retries completely so that the job fails fast and reports the error
Show the answer

Answer: C. Exponential backoff with jitter spreads retries, and the SDKs do it by default; if throttling continues the cause is capacity or a hot key, so adjust provisioned throughput, on-demand mode or the key design.

S7Which statement about AWS DMS is correct?

  • AIt supports full load, change data capture, or both, between different engines
  • BIt can only copy data between two databases that run the same engine, and it cannot keep them in sync
  • CIt converts application code but does not move any data between stores
  • DIt runs only on premises and cannot write to Amazon S3 or Amazon Redshift
Show the answer

Answer: A. DMS is a managed replication service that supports full load, CDC and both, and supports heterogeneous migrations. Schema conversion is a separate feature.

10Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Source → tool SaaS AppFlow; database DMS; S3 files Glue / EMR / Lambda; SFTP Transfer Family; on-premises files DataSync; offline Snow Family
DMS Full load, CDC, or both; heterogeneous moves; KMS at rest, SSL in flight
AppFlow No code; on demand, schedule or event; mask, filter, partition; PrivateLink
Incremental Glue job bookmarks (default disabled; S3 by last-modified time; JDBC by sequential key), DMS CDC
Redshift load COPY from S3; splittable files split at 128 MB; unsplittable: 1 MB to 1 GB files, multiple of slices
Schedule EventBridge Scheduler (recommended), scheduled rules (legacy, ≥ 1 minute), Glue scheduled and conditional triggers, MWAA
cron 6 fields (min, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week, year); ? in one day field; UTC
Event S3 notifications to SNS, SQS, Lambda, EventBridge; at least once; avoid same-bucket loops; FIFO via EventBridge
Allowlist NAT gateway + Elastic IP; DMS instance in the source's security group; PrivateLink
Throttling Exponential backoff with jitter, stop near 1 minute, add capacity, spread keys, buffer with SQS; API Gateway 10,000 rps / 5,000 burst
